items.title: آنچه گذشت؛ آمریکا برای اطلاعات درباره برنامه هسته‌ای ایران تا ۲۰ میلیون دلار پاداش تعیین کرد
items.summary: وزارت خارجه آمریکا در فراخوانی عمومی برای دریافت اطلاعات درباره برنامه هسته‌ای ایران، از جمله دانشمندان، تاسیسات و فناوری‌های مرتبط با آن، تا سقف ۲۰ میلیون دلار پاداش تعیین کرده است. برنامه «پاداش برای عدالت» آمریکا می‌گوید که دولت آن کشور همچنان به مقابله با هرگونه تلاش ایران برای توسعه تسلیحات هسته‌ای متعهد است. این برنامه زیر نظر سرویس امنیت دیپلماتیک وزارت خارجه آمریکا فعالیت می‌کند و پیش‌تر نیز برای دریافت اطلاعات درباره شبکه‌های فروش و انتقال نفت ایران، فرماندهان نیروی هوافضای سپاه پاسداران و عوامل مرتبط با فعالیت‌های سایبری این نیرو پاداش تعیین کرده بود.

items.title: آمریکا کارگروه ویژه‌ای در ارتباط با مرزهای زمینی ایران و دریای خزر تشکیل می‌دهد
items.summary: پس از ماه‌ها محاصره دریایی ایران، فرماندهی مرکزی ارتش آمریکا دستور تشکیل یک کارگروه ویژه را صادر کرده که هدف آن محدود کردن جابه‌جایی سامانه‌های تسلیحاتی پیشرفته و دیگر اقلام تحریمی ایران از طریق مرزهای زمینی و دریای خزر است. سپاه پاسداران اعلام کرده«محدودیت برد موشک‌ها» برای این نیرو برداشته شده و وزیر خارجه قطر گفته «مسئله ایران نمی‌تواند بدون راه‌حل باقی بماند.»

items.title: سازمان ملل متحد می‌گوید که انتظار می‌رود تا پایان امسال «۷۰۰ مرکز درمانی» در افغانستان بسته شود

items.summary_original: At least a dozen California district attorneys are publicly condemning Gov. Gavin Newsom’s plan to commute all 548 death sentences in the state, arguing the sweeping move overrides juries, disregards victims’ families and defies the will of state voters. Newsom announced the plan Thursday, saying state-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California’s values. The move would convert the sentences to life without parole, though 382 cases still require approval from at least four California Supreme Court justices, according to the Associated Press. In response, prosecuting attorneys across California have raised concerns about victims’ rights, the governor’s constitutional authority and the role of the California Supreme Court in reviewing hundreds of the commutations. "Justice requires case-by-case consideration, not one-size-fits-all decisions," Sacramento County District Attorney Thien Ho said in response to Newsom's action. THREE STATES CARRY OUT EXECUTIONS ON SAME DAY AMID RENEWED DEATH PENALTY DEBATE Orange County District Attorney Todd Spitzer described the move as "mercy for the wolves" that inflicts "the ultimate act of cruelty on the sheep." Spitzer noted that regulations implemented by California’s Board of Parole Hearings on Oct. 1 allow thousands of prisoners serving life without parole to become eligible for parole, arguing that Newsom's latest death row commutations could put these inmates "one step closer" to release. items.summary_original: EXCLUSIVE: A group of Minnesota Republican state lawmakers asked the IRS in August 2019 to "conduct a detailed reexamination" of tax filings by Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., based on a report from a state board suggesting she filed joint tax returns in 2014 and 2015 with a man she was not legally married to, according to a letter obtained by Fox News Digital. The letter was sent after the Minnesota Campaign Finance and Public Disclosure Board issued a report on June 6, 2019, indicating that Omar had filed joint tax returns in 2014 and 2015 with Ahmed Hirsi, despite being legally married to another man, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, at the time. The joint tax returns came up during the Minnesota Campaign Finance and Public Disclosure Board’s examination of a $1,500 expense associated with Omar’s campaign committee. The board was investigating whether the expenditure was a legitimate campaign-related expense or whether campaign funds had been used to pay for services that benefited Omar personally. The payment was part of a larger $2,250 reimbursement to the Kjellberg Law Office for legal and other services. items.summary_original: District attorneys and law enforcement unions across California have publicly condemned Gov. Gavin Newsom following his announcement to commute the sentences of 548 death row inmates, a decision one prosecutor called a slap in the face to victims' families. Newsom’s sweeping order to commute the condemned inmates to life in prison without the possibility of parole has drawn intense criticism alongside praise from anti-death penalty advocates. "I think it's all about politics, sadly. Politics is over people in this case, and that's a real sad state of affairs," San Luis Obispo County District Attorney Dan Dow told Fox News Digital. ALABAMA GOVERNOR COMMUTES DEATH SENTENCE AS DOUBTS EMERGE ABOUT EVIDENCE IN MURDER CONVICTION In an open letter detailing his decision, Newsom said California's capital punishment system is fundamentally at odds with the state's principles. "After nearly 30 years in public office, I have come to understand the limits of what government can justly accomplish," Newsom wrote. "I take this action because I firmly believe that state-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California’s values, undermines the foundations of our legal system, and diminishes each of us." POPE LEO DENOUNCES DEATH PENALTY AS 'INADMISSIBLE' AHEAD OF PENTAGON'S PLANNED LIVESTREAMED EXECUTION Upon taking office in 2019, Newsom issued an executive moratorium on capital punishment . "Long ago, you predicted that you would win this race by seven points, which at the time seemed like a pretty cocky and ill-considered thing to say. Then you won the race by seven points. People are still calling you cocky," podcast host Jon Favreau said during his interview with El-Sayed. "How do you see yourself?" "I think there is a responsibility that we have to engage with [Trump] as the unserious fool that he is," El-Sayed replied. It also raises questions of whether El-Sayed’s campaign strategies will yield results in Congress. In his view, Trump has changed the style of acceptable communication. In turn, he accused Democrats of being hesitant to abandon a kind of decorum to fight fire with fire. items.summary_original: Republican control of the Senate could return as soon as the 2028 general election, but only if the party can pull off a series of crucial victories in competitive races, a possibility that seems distant following Tuesday night's devastating Democratic sweep. As of publication, Democrats and independents who caucus with them have secured 54 Senate seats, a total that could grow to as many as 56 pending election calls in Mississippi and Alaska. Assuming Republicans hold the vice presidency in 2028, far from a guarantee, they would need to flip at least four seats during that election cycle to win the Senate back. While there are ample pick-up opportunities for Republicans in 2028 if the party can return to its typical national performance benchmarks, several vulnerable GOP-held seats could complicate their efforts to retake the upper chamber. DEMS FLIPS YET ANOTHER SENATE SEAT IN TRUMP COUNTRY AMID SWEEPING GOP UPSETS Iowa Sen. Chuck Grassley, for instance, turned 93 in September and faces a decision about whether to seek another term in 2028, when Republicans will be defending his seat in a state where Democrat Josh Turek just defeated Republican Ashley Hinson by roughly four percentage points. His departure before then could also give Iowa's incoming Democratic governor the opportunity to appoint a temporary replacement. items.summary_original: Some troops have gone a year without hot water. Others are sleeping in their cars to escape barracks without air conditioning. And some are asking for little more than drywall, spackle and paint so they can make repairs themselves. Those are among the conditions Medal of Honor recipient Dakota Meyer says he has encountered while touring military installations on a mission from War Secretary Pete Hegseth : Fix a barracks system plagued by decades of neglect. "I would tell you that there's only a couple that I've seen that are good," Meyer told Fox News Digital in an interview Thursday. Meyer, who serves as senior adviser to the Pentagon's Barracks Task Force, has visited more than eight installations across the Army, Navy, Air Force and Marine Corps since taking on the assignment and plans to visit 30 before the end of the year. "What I thought was gonna be a professional job very quickly turned into personal," Meyer said. "If she could just have a hot shower," Meyer recalled. "It's absolutely heartbreaking." The Pentagon's barracks problems long predate Hegseth and have survived repeated attempts at reform. items.summary: دو شهردار سوسیالیست روز سه شنبه در لس آنجلس و واشنگتن دی سی در ایالات متحده انتخاب شدند که اکنون به این معنی است که چهار شهر از 20 شهر بزرگ این کشور دارای رهبران سوسیالیست هستند. نیتیا رامان، عضو شورای لس آنجلس، یکی از اعضای سوسیالیست های دموکرات آمریکا (DSA) شهردار فعلی کارن باس را شکست داد و در ماه دسامبر به عنوان شهردار تقریباً 4 میلیون نفر از ساکنان لس آنجلس کار خواهد کرد. همچنین روز سه‌شنبه، جینیز لوئیس جورج، عضو DSA، پیروز شد که با پیروزی به شهردار منتخب واشنگتن دی سی، شهری با جمعیتی حدود 700000 نفر رسید. فهرست شهرداران سوسیالیست در 20 شهر پرجمعیت ایالات متحده در 4 شهر قرار دارد، زیرا جورج و رامان به شهردار سیاتل، کیتی ویلسون و شهردار نیویورک، زهران ممدانی پیوستند. سوسیالیست دموکرات
items.summary_original: Two socialist mayors were elected in the United States on Tuesday in Los Angeles and Washington, D.C. which now means that four of the top 20 largest cities in the country have socialist leaders at the helm. Los Angeles Councilwoman Nithya Raman, a member of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) defeated incumbent mayor Karen Bass and will take office in December as mayor for the roughly 4 million residents of Los Angeles proper. Also victorious on Tuesday was DSA member Janeese Lewis George who coasted to victory to become mayor-elect of Washington, D.C., a city of roughly 700,000 residents. The list of socialist mayors in the top 20 most populous U.S. cities stands at 4, as George and Raman join Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani. DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST SWEEPS INTO DC MAYOR'S OFFICE, SIGNALS OPENNESS TO WORKING WITH TRUMP In total, the four cities are home to roughly 14 million people. That figure does not include neighboring suburbs, which could still feel the effects of policies enacted within city limits through crime, real estate values and the broader business climate. Problems in a city can spill over into surrounding communities, while suburban residents who work in the city may also be directly affected. Counting the population in the metro areas of those four cities, roughly 44 million people could be affected either positively and negatively by the socialist policies enacted by the four mayors. DOGE یک فاجعه برای آمریکا بود، و من کاملا مطمئن هستم که حداقل یک کمیته در مورد آن تحقیق خواهد کرد. باید در مورد آن تحقیق کند. ماسک به عنوان یک هدف بالقوه برای نظارت دموکرات ها ظاهر شده است و برخی از قانونگذاران خواستار بررسی دقیق زمان او به عنوان رئیس DOGE هستند. درخواست ها برای انجام تحقیقات در حالی مطرح می شود که دموکرات ها پس از پیروزی در اواسط، حزب را برای بررسی فساد در دولت ترامپ آغاز کرده اند.
items.summary_original: Rep. Jamie Raskin, D-Md., and Gov. JB Pritzker , D-Ill., are calling for an investigation into the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), previously led by Elon Musk, as talks have heated up among Democrats to launch a probe into the multibillionaire. "I had no specific plan," Raskin told Fox News Digital about the potential investigations . "Look…DOGE was a catastrophe for America, and at least one committee, I feel pretty certain, will investigate it. It needs to investigate it." Musk has emerged as a potential target of Democratic oversight, with some lawmakers calling for scrutiny of his time as head of the DOGE. The calls for an investigation come as Democrats have started rallying the party to look into corruption under the Trump administration after coming out victorious in midterms . SCHUMER, JEFFRIES SIDESTEP QUESTIONS ON NUKING FILIBUSTER, LAUNCHING ELON MUSK PROBE AFTER BLUE WAVE The tech CEO helped launch DOGE at the start of President Donald Trump 's second term to root out waste and be more transparent about the federal government's spending. DOGE's efforts included deferred resignations and buyouts of employees at federal agencies and contributed to a significant downsizing of the federal workforce , which contracted by about 250,000 employees during 2025, according to the Government Accountability Office (GAO). Calls for investigations into DOGE also started over concerns about the department allegedly having access to Americans’ sensitive information . "

items.summary_original: DUBAI, United Arab Emirates — A senior United Arab Emirates official says he is cautiously optimistic about negotiations between the United States and Iran, citing progress through Qatari mediation over the past days, even as fears of renewed military confrontation continue to grip the Middle East . "We see some progress. … We hope that both sides will be able to reach a point where they will start building trust and engaging in a way to avoid the war, to find a political solution. … I am a little bit optimistic, but I don't exclude the other option," Dr. Ali Rashid Al Nuaimi, chairman of the Defense, Interior and Foreign Affairs Committee of the UAE's Federal National Council, told Fox News Digital in an exclusive interview. His remarks came as Reuters reported on Nov. 5 that Iran had submitted a new nuclear proposal to Washington through Qatar. Tehran, however, continued to insist that the U.S. meet seven conditions before negotiations could proceed, including sanctions relief and an end to the American naval blockade. IS THIS TRUMP’S LAST ‘LAST CHANCE’? CEASELESS STRING OF BROKEN CEASEFIRES FUELS DOUBT OVER IRAN DEAL President Donald Trump has not ruled out further military operations, while Iran has threatened broader retaliation if fighting resumes. For the UAE, which endured thousands of Iranian missile and drone attacks earlier this year, the possibility of a diplomatic breakthrough offers hope. "فقط تلاش رقت انگیز دیگری برای جمع آوری کلیک. البته با استفاده از منابع ناشناس!" او افزود. روزنامه پست روز جمعه با استناد به سه نفری که در مورد برنامه‌های او توضیح داده بودند، گزارش داد که دیسانتیس در حال آماده شدن برای نامزدی ریاست جمهوری جمهوری‌خواه در سال 2028 است.
items.summary_original: Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis fired back Friday at a report that he is preparing another White House bid in 2028, accusing The Washington Post of fabricating claims that he has started reaching out to political consultants about a potential campaign. "The Washington Post is fabricating this out of whole cloth," DeSantis wrote on X. "I have not reached out to anybody about running for anything." "Just another pathetic attempt to garner clicks. Using anonymous sources of course!" he added. The Post reported Friday, citing three people briefed on his plans, that DeSantis was preparing to seek the Republican presidential nomination in 2028. VANCE, CRUZ AND DESANTIS DIAGNOSE GOP'S MIDTERM DISASTER AS BATTLE OVER PARTY'S FUTURE BEGINS The newspaper reported that DeSantis, who unsuccessfully ran for president in 2024 and is term-limited after 2026, had already reached out to at least one national political consultant about working on a prospective campaign. A federal super PAC tied to DeSantis also sent out a fundraising text earlier this week, The Post reported. DeSantis continued pushing back against the report in exchanges with social media users. When one user expressed hope that The Post's reporting was accurate, the governor replied that he was "sorry to disappoint." DeSantis also responded to another user who suggested political consultants may have been using his name to attract attention. "Probably the case. But maybe just made up by WaPo," he wrote. items.summary_original: The U.S. is offering up to $20 million to anyone with information on Iran’s nuclear program. "If you have information on Iran’s nuclear program, assets, or associated individuals, send it to us via Signal or our Tor-based tip line. You may be eligible for a reward and relocation," the U.S. Department of State’s Rewards for Justice program said in an announcement posted to X. The State Department said it was seeking information on "nuclear scientists and staff, nuclear program-related technologies, and capabilities, associated organizations and personnel." EXPERTS ‘DEEPLY’ CONCERNED OVER IRAN’S WORK AT UNDERGROUND NUCLEAR SITE "The U.S. government remains committed to countering any attempt by Iran to develop a nuclear weapons program," the agency added. The announcement comes as President Donald Trump considers renewed military strikes against Iran while Washington and Tehran continue negotiations over the country's nuclear program. IRANIAN NEGOTIATORS KICKED OUT OF US AS TALKS STALL; TRUMP LAYS OUT 'POSSIBLE' TIMELINE FOR MORE STRIKES Trump reiterated Friday that Iran would never be permitted to obtain a nuclear weapon, pointing to previous U.S. military operations targeting Tehran's nuclear facilities . The president met with his national security team Thursday to consider renewing military strikes against Iran after Trump promised to wait until after the midterms. items.summary_original: President Donald Trump highlighted NASA's ambitious plans to launch its first nuclear-powered spacecraft to Mars within the next two years, reaffirming his administration's push to expand American space exploration and eventually send astronauts to the red planet. Speaking at the UP Summit at Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Florida, Trump touted the mission as part of his administration's broader ambitions to expand America's presence beyond Earth. "Within the next two years, NASA will launch the first-ever nuclear-powered spacecraft to Mars ," Trump said. The president described the mission as a step toward eventually sending American astronauts to the planet. TRUMP CALLS ISS CREW FROM HOUSTON TO PRAISE SPACE PIONEERS AND OFFER 'OVAL OFFICE TIME' "We're going to be paving the way for astronauts to plant the Stars and Stripes on the red planet," he said. The planned mission comes as NASA's Artemis program aims to establish a long-term human presence on the moon before eventually sending astronauts to Mars. Earlier this year, astronauts completed a lunar flyby during the Artemis II mission. Artemis III is scheduled to test spacecraft and landing systems in Earth orbit in 2027, while Artemis IV is expected to attempt a lunar landing in early 2028, before the end of Trump's presidential term. items.summary_original: The midterms are over. But even more pitched battles are underway. These are internal House and Senate leadership elections. House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., won’t pursue the minority leader post. President Trump doesn’t always see eye-to-eye with Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., but the president hasn’t demanded a change there. Some incoming House and Senate progressives have expressed their reservations about House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., and Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., despite the stunning Democratic wins from Tuesday night. REPORTER’S NOTEBOOK: A DEMOCRATIC MAJORITY COULD EXPOSE THE LIMITS OF THE PROGRESSIVE AGENDA Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed, D-Mich., has long warned he might not support Schumer for Majority Leader. "If you’re Chuck Schumer, I’m dangerous," El-Sayed advised in late June. The Michigan Democrat ducked the question when asked about supporting Schumer on NBC just after the election. "I am going to vote for the option that gives me the best chance of getting money out of politics. Putting money in pockets and passing Medicare for all," said El-Sayed. "I'm interested to see, working with the rest of our caucus, what options we've got." By Thursday on CNN, El-Sayed was reiterating his support for Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., who hasn’t announced he’s running for anything. "I think he'd be an amazing Senate majority leader," said El-Sayed of Van Hollen. items.summary_original: President Donald Trump tapped Stephen Miller to succeed Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff , elevating an adviser who reportedly helped develop plans to advance his agenda without congressional approval as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress in January. Miller, Office of Management and Budget Director Russell Vought and White House lawyers have worked since April to identify executive actions Trump could take without new legislation, including measures on immigration, tariffs, housing costs and federal spending, Reuters reported Sunday, citing three people familiar with the planning. With Democrats set to control Congress in January, Trump will face greater obstacles to passing legislation, while Democratic lawmakers will gain the power to launch investigations into his administration. items.summary_original: The Democratic mayor of America's fourth-largest city is reversing course on cooperation with federal immigration authorities despite an executive order from defeated Texas Republican Gov. Greg Abbott that threatened the loss of millions in state funding for noncompliance. The Lone Star State swung blue for the first time since its new senator-elect, James Talarico, was born, and Houston Mayor John Whitmire wasted no time Friday announcing new restrictions on cooperation with ICE. Whitmire told The New York Times that city police are not permitted to notify ICE if they encounter an illegal immigrant in "nonviolent contacts" like traffic stops or minor offenses. 'WE DIDN'T EXPECT THIS': TEXAS DEMOCRATS STUNNED AS BLUE WAVE TOPPLES GOP STRONGHOLD "If they’re charged with a new crime, we’ll let ICE know as we get them to the jailhouse," he told the paper Friday. Abbott lost his bid for a fourth term Tuesday, and Talarico flipped one of the state’s Senate seats blue for the first time since Clinton Treasury Secretary Lloyd Bentsen won his final re-election bid in 1988 — seven months before the current senator-elect was born. Texas’ most recent Democratic governor, Ann Richards, the mother of former longtime Planned Parenthood president Cecile Richards, was elected shortly thereafter in 1990. items.summary_original: Internal party House and Senate leadership elections are some of the most fascinating exercises that unfold on Capitol Hill. Both House and Senate Democrats and House and Senate Republicans will choose their leaders in the coming days. And the changes are going to be seismic. But not everyone is on board with heir apparent leaders. That’s what makes this process so intriguing. However, there are only two rules in leadership elections: You can’t beat someone with no one. And, perhaps more importantly, it’s about the math. PROGRESSIVES FUME AT HAKEEM JEFFRIES FOR SAYING DEMOCRATS WON'T 'GET EVEN' WITH TRUMP There are some progressives and DSA-affiliated Democrats who will be House Members next year who want someone other than House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y. Who? Well, no one has said. Again, you can’t beat someone with no one. And, frankly, it’s hard to believe that Democrats would not elect the first Black speaker of the House. But drill down on the math. For the sake of argument, let’s say Democrats have 260 House seats in the new Congress. First, Democrats must tap a nominee for speaker in their caucus. That needs a simple majority. So, surely Jeffries will score at least 131 votes in a private ballot for speaker. "I still am on [the committee on] foreign affairs and I’ve taken a particular interest in peace deals as well as supporting the administration’s peace deal efforts. And I want my constituency to understand when I’m either talking on these things or advocating for them in Washington, that I am controlled by no one, influenced by no one," Luna said in a video posted to X. Luna’s announcement comes on the heels of devastating midterm results for Republicans that have sparked debate about the role of pro-Israel political spending and U.S. policy toward Israel in several Democratic campaigns. items.summary_original: Russia played a larger role in the Iran war than previously disclosed, with internal defense industry documents revealing how Moscow built up the country's arsenal ahead of its conflict with the U.S. A Russian contract is tied to 90 launchers for precision-guided missiles with the destination as Tehran, according to documents obtained and published by Ukrainian defense intelligence research group Dallas Analytics offering new details on the extent of Moscow's military support for Iran before war erupted. President Donald Trump has repeatedly downplayed Russia's role in the conflict — as recently as last month, saying that he did not believe they are helping Iran "at all." IRAN TAPS FINANCIAL LIFELINE, RUSSIAN ARMS AS TRUMP ESCALATES 'CRUSHING' ECONOMIC WARFARE Russian production records show components were allocated for 90 APU-L twin-rail launchers under a contract identified as "K-10," with shipments within the Russian production chain scheduled from late 2024 through December 2025. Other internal Russian documents obtained by Dallas Analytics explicitly identify "K-10" as Iran. An October 2022 supply request for equipment for a Yak-130 aircraft lists the consignee as "'K10' Iran" and was countersigned by the acting head of the Russian Defense Ministry's 704th Military Representation. Tim Moore in North Carolina’s 14th Congressional District race, Democrat LaKesha Womack is set to appear in court on a pending felony charge. Womack secured 51.1% of the vote in the House race, while Moore received 48.9%, according to election results reported by The Associated Press. The Mecklenburg County Sheriff’s Office previously confirmed to Fox News Digital that Womack had been served a criminal summons on Oct. 11 by a deputy with the Polk County Sheriff’s Office on a pending felony charge alleging she failed to return a rental vehicle valued at $20,000 in 2019. The criminal summons was issued in January 2020 but not served until 2026, according to WBTV. Womack is set to appear in court on Nov. 10, The New York Post reported Thursday. items.summary_original: On a night when Democrats made major gains across the country, South Dakota emerged as one of the few Republican strongholds where the GOP largely held its ground — even as Democrats made inroads around Sioux Falls. Republican Gov. Larry Rhoden won roughly 63.5% of the vote Tuesday, nearly matching President Donald Trump's 63.4% performance in 2024. Republicans also swept the state's other statewide races and maintained overwhelming control of the legislature, despite Democrats picking up four seats. Rhoden's victory came against Democrat Dan Ahlers, who described himself as a "conservative Democrat" and campaigned on affordability, rural healthcare, education and other kitchen table issues. But his moderate pitch did little to narrow the GOP's commanding statewide advantage, with Ahlers finishing at just 36.5% of the vote. South Dakota's results stood in contrast to several other deeply Republican states where the GOP maintained control but saw its margins shrink considerably. In Idaho and Wyoming, Republican gubernatorial candidates won comfortably but finished with smaller shares of the vote than President Donald Trump secured in 2024. South Dakota's gubernatorial result, by comparison, remained virtually unchanged. items.summary_original: John Eisenberg, the head of the National Security Division at the Department of Justice , is stepping down from his post, becoming the third senior DOJ official to resign since the midterm elections. Shortly after Fox News learned of Eisenberg's resignation, Attorney General Todd Blanche announced it on social media. "He has served with distinction, strengthening our nation’s ability to address threats, both foreign and domestic," Blanche said. "Under his leadership, the Division advanced President Trump’s mission to make America safe by prosecuting terrorists and working with our law enforcement partners to disrupt planned attacks on the American people." This was Eisenberg's second stint serving under President Donald Trump . In Trump's first term, Eisenberg was an assistant and deputy counsel to the president, as well as a legal advisor to the National Security Council, which advises presidents on foreign policy matters. DOJ CIVIL RIGHTS CHIEF HARMEET DHILLON RESIGNS, SAYS WHITE HOUSE ASKED HER TO WAIT UNTIL AFTER MIDTERMS Less than an hour before Eisenberg's departure was made public, Blanche announced the resignation of Jason Reding Quiñones, the U.S. Attorney for Florida's Southern District. Quiñones was perhaps best known for securing an indictment against Raúl Castro , the former president of Cuba who took over after his brother Fidel Castro's nearly 50-year reign. items.summary_original: Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., plans to reintroduce articles of impeachment for Pentagon Chief Pete Hegseth next week. The chances are increasingly high that the House could in fact impeach Hegseth. Why? Massie tried to impeach Hegseth before the midterms. But the House adjourned a day early in September, nixing Massie’s effort. House Speaker Mike Johnson , R-La., condemned the effort by Massie. But insisted that he didn’t send members home early because of fear that the House had the votes to impeach Hegseth. So Massie’s articles of impeachment expired. But he will reintroduce them next week. Under the rules, the House must consider them within two days. THE HITCHHIKER’S GUIDE TO MASSIE SAYING JOHNSON IS SENDING THE HOUSE HOME EARLY TO PREVENT HEGSETH IMPEACHMENT It’s possible the House could move to table the articles, or send them to committee, euthanizing the effort. But a growing number of House Republicans have grumbled about Hegseth. Any effort to dismiss the articles in the House might not work. It’s about the math. All Democrats are likely to vote to impeach. There are some Republicans who have said privately they’d like to impeach. Now, after the midterms, you have more Republicans hoping to build distance between themselves and President Trump. Moreover, the war in Iran contributed directly to the GOP’s thumping. items.summary_original: Michigan voters approved a ballot initiative called Proposal 2, pitched to them as a way to curb pay-to-play donations and get money out of politics. But the measure has also triggered a federal First Amendment lawsuit alleging its separate speech and disclosure provisions could ensnare journalists, nonprofits and policy researchers who discuss elected officials. Michiganders for Money Out of Politics, also known as MOP UP Michigan, said the lawsuit was expected after voters approved Proposal 2. Campaign manager Maura Cowley said the group is "confident Proposal 2 will withstand legal scrutiny" after organizers said they submitted more than 560,000 signatures to place the measure on the ballot. The Mackinac Center for Public Policy, which filed the lawsuit, says it is not challenging the initiative’s central pay-to-play restrictions on political contributions from utility companies and government contractors. Its lawsuit instead targets provisions imposing reporting and disclosure requirements on certain communications that refer to candidates or "promote, support, attack or oppose" candidates or ballot questions, even without expressly urging voters to support or oppose them. "Michigan voters deserve the freedom to research, debate, and report on the policies that shape their lives. items.summary: ابوظبی، امارات متحده عربی — در افتتاحیه بزرگترین کنفرانس انرژی جهان در ابوظبی، هوش مصنوعی در کنار نفت و گاز در کانون توجه قرار گرفت زیرا سام آلتمن، مدیر عامل OpenAI به مقامات ارشد امارات متحده عربی برای اعلام همکاری بزرگی با هدف ورود هوش مصنوعی پیشرفته به صنعت انرژی پیوست. مراسم افتتاحیه ADIPEC 2026 با حضور فاکس نیوز دیجیتال، مقامات ارشد دولتی و رهبران صنعت انرژی را در زمانی گرد هم آورد که جنگ با ایران و اختلال در تنگه هرمز فشار فوق‌العاده‌ای بر عرضه جهانی انرژی وارد کرده است. اما در میان بحث در مورد تولید نفت، مسیرهای کشتیرانی و امنیت انرژی، دکتر سلطان الجابر، وزیر صنعت و فناوری پیشرفته امارات متحده عربی و مدیر اجرایی انرژی دولتی
items.summary_original: ABU DHABI, United Arab Emirates — At the opening of the world's largest energy conference in Abu Dhabi, artificial intelligence took center stage alongside oil and gas as OpenAI CEO Sam Altman joined senior UAE officials for the announcement of a major partnership aimed at bringing advanced AI into the energy industry. The opening ceremony of ADIPEC 2026, attended by Fox News Digital, brought together senior government officials and energy industry leaders at a time when the war involving Iran and disruptions to the Strait of Hormuz have placed extraordinary pressure on global energy supplies. But amid discussions about oil production, shipping routes and energy security, Dr. Sultan Al Jaber, the UAE’s minister of industry and advanced technology and chief executive of state-owned energy giant ADNOC, delivered a different challenge to the technology industry. OIL SQUEEZE TIGHTENS AS IRAN-BACKED ATTACKS CRIPPLE HORMUZ ESCAPE ROUTES "From the moment ChatGPT was born, the world has asked what energy can do for AI. And now, together, we will find out what AI can do for energy," Al Jaber told the audience, introducing a partnership between ADNOC, OpenAI and Abu Dhabi-based technology company G42. The announcement marked a significant step in the UAE’s ambition to become a global center for artificial intelligence, using its energy resources, financial strength and growing partnerships with American technology companies to help shape the industry’s future. items.summary_original: First lady Melania Trump and envoys from both Russia and Ukraine spoke from the White House on Thursday, hailing the ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Oleshky region as a potential "spark" for peace that lasts beyond a temporary regional ceasefire. "We have chosen humanity over war," the first lady said in a White House trilateral news conference with the two warring countries. "Undeniably, the lives of innocent people must transcend the division of war. I hope Oleshky inspires greater peace. Every significant transformation begins with a small spark." "Together, we can create something more enduring than a temporary ceasefire," she added, calling Oleshky "a spark in a world of darkness capable of illuminating the best in humanity." INSIDE MELANIA TRUMP'S SECRET DIPLOMATIC ROLE IN THE RUSSIA-UKRAINE CEASEFIRE DEAL Trump said she became aware of a humanitarian crisis in the region in September and directed her representative, Marc Beckman, to engage with Russia and Ukraine on her behalf. She said both countries agreed to work with her as an "exclusive intermediary" to establish a ceasefire in Oleshky and the surrounding Kherson region, deliver humanitarian aid and create a safe evacuation route for civilians. Her remarks were followed by comments from Russian special envoy Kirill Dmitriev , who said Russian President Vladimir Putin appreciated President Donald Trump’s efforts to stop the fighting. items.summary_original: France deployed 70,000 police officers Thursday as tens of thousands of people took to the streets for nationwide strikes and protests after left-wing groups called for a mobilization. In Paris, the Eiffel Tower was closed; in Lyon, French riot police fired tear gas and charged a group of protesters; and near Toulouse, a high school was set on fire, according to Reuters. "We need to turn up in big numbers on the streets today," the news agency quoted the head of the left-wing CGT union Sophie Binet as saying. The demonstrations come after France was rocked by violent protests in October, which outgoing French President Emmanuel Macron blamed on "ultra-left groups whose aim is to bring down the Republic." FRANCE'S MACRON BLAMES PROTESTS ON 'ULTRA-LEFT GROUPS WHOSE AIM IS TO BRING DOWN THE REPUBLIC' An official close to Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said that by early Thursday, around 270,000 people had joined the union action in 180 rallies outside the capital. About a third of France’s high schools were closed or unable to operate, some because of student blockades and others because teachers were on strike, The Associated Press reported. Toby Harris, an Australian tourist who was visiting Paris on Thursday, told Fox News Digital that "I feel like it's probably a good thing that there's like political action in the city. items.summary_original: Multiple planes across Europe were diverted and forced to make emergency landings Thursday because of bomb threats that have turned out to be unfounded. At least 11 planes, originating from cities including Copenhagen, Dublin, Helsinki, Madrid, Milan and Warsaw, have been affected. The source of the threats was not immediately clear. These incidents came after several flights in Europe received similar warnings on Tuesday that the U.K. government described as "malicious hoax threats." "Upon receiving a threat regarding the placement of an improvised explosive device on board 4 aircraft heading to Prague, we are preparing with colleagues from Prague Airport for their landing. We assess the relevance of the threats as low," Czech Police wrote on X, before adding that inspections of the planes yielded "negative results." The threats come at a time when European officials have been blaming Russia and Iran for "hybrid attacks" and acts of sabotage, which both Moscow and Tehran deny, Reuters reported. items.summary_original: A U.S. Marine died Tuesday after an incident during training at Camp Schwab in Okinawa, Japan, military officials said. The incident happened in Okinawa, on a Marine Corps base near the northeastern coast of Okinawa Prefecture. The Marine, who was identified as Lance Cpl. Devin J. Hernandez, 25, of Maryland, was with the 3rd Marine Division. "We express our deepest condolences to the family and loved ones of our Marine." Hernandez was participating in fast-rope training at Camp Schwab when he sustained injuries during the training, the 3rd Marine Division said in a later statement to Fox News Digital. He was transported to a hospital and later succumbed to his injuries. "A Marine currently assigned to 3rd Marine Division was involved in a fast rope training incident at Camp Schwab on Nov. 3, 2026. items.summary: به گفته مقامات، یک زن کانادایی و دخترش در یک حمله مشکوک خرس گریزلی در آخر هفته هنگام پیاده روی در مسیری نزدیک خانه خود کشته شدند. جنیفر بالکاراس، 48 ساله، هنردرمانگر، و دخترش، سله رید، 20 ساله، روز شنبه پس از رفتن به پیاده روی در مسیر Snooka West Trail، تنها چند دقیقه از خانه خود در بلا کولا، بریتیش کلمبیا، ناپدید شدند. برادرش مت بالکاراس به The Vancouver Sun گفت که وقتی بالکاراس در یک جلسه آنلاین برنامه ریزی شده در روز شنبه حاضر نشد، عزیزان نگران شدند. راهنمای عملی برای اینکه خرس در تابستان امسال در حین پیاده‌روی یا کمپینگ مورد حمله قرار نگیرید پس از اینکه نتوانستند به این جفت برسند، بستگان از پلیس سواره سلطنتی کانادا (RCMP) خواستند تا یک بررسی رفاهی را در صبح یکشنبه انجام دهند. مقامات خودروی بالکاراس را که در آن پارک شده بود کشف کردند
items.summary_original: A Canadian woman and her daughter were killed in a suspected grizzly bear attack over the weekend while hiking on a trail near their home, according to authorities. Jennifer Balcarras, 48, an art therapist, and her daughter, Selah Reed, 20, went missing Saturday after going for a walk on the Snooka West Trail, just minutes from their home in Bella Coola, British Columbia . Loved ones grew concerned when Balcarras failed to show up for a scheduled online meet-up on Saturday, her brother, Matt Balcarras, told The Vancouver Sun . A PRACTICAL GUIDE TO NOT GETTING MAULED BY A BEAR WHILE HIKING OR CAMPING THIS SUMMER After failing to reach the pair, relatives asked the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) for a welfare check on Sunday morning. Authorities discovered Balcarras' vehicle parked at the trailhead . Her body was recovered Monday, and search teams found Reed's body on Tuesday. GRIZZLY BEAR MAULS HIKER, DRAGS HIM DOZENS OF FEET ON GLACIER NATIONAL PARK TRAIL "There was evidence to suggest a bear may have been involved," Jeff Tyre, an inspector with the British Columbia Conservation Officer Service, said in a video update posted to social media. Tyre noted that officers were actively working to "locate and capture any bears involved" and said it was not immediately clear if more than one animal was responsible. items.summary_original: After crushing powerful criminal gangs in El Salvador, President Nayib Bukele has turned his attention to the Caribbean nation of Haiti, deploying 2,000 troops after four Salvadoran military aviation technicians disappeared following an Oct.18 ambush near Port-au-Prince. "We have already finished with the gangs in El Salvador, and we can finish with you too," Bukele wrote in a message on X directed at Haiti's criminal groups. Bukele stressed that the operation's objective was not to invade Haiti or conduct a long-term occupation, but to recover the four missing Salvadorans alive. The disappearance has become a national priority for Bukele, who has warned Haitian gang leaders that El Salvador is prepared to use overwhelming force if the men are not returned alive. FLORIDA JURY CONVICTS 4 MEN WHO PLOTTED ASSASSINATION OF HAITI'S PRESIDENT FROM SOUTH FLORIDA HUB The aviation technicians were assigned to a medical unit as part of the United Nations -backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF) in Haiti when their armored vehicle was attacked in Croix-des-Bouquets. Haiti’s National Police announced Tuesday, more than two weeks after the attack, that it had found the charred remains of the vehicle in the Santo neighborhood of Croix-des-Bouquets. Police said, however, they found no sign of the missing men. El Salvador says the men were abducted, the Haitian government says the soldiers are missing, and one gang leader says they are dead. items.summary_original: TEL AVIV, Israel: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s hold on power in Israel will be tested Wednesday as President Isaac Herzog begins consultations with leaders of all parties elected to the 26th Knesset before deciding which lawmaker to task with forming the next government. The final vote count, published last Friday by Israel's Central Elections Committee, gave Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, compared with 48 for the opposition alliance led by Gadi Eisenkot — 61 seats are needed to form a government. On Monday, Netanyahu posted to X that "the public in Israel does not want a government that depends on Ra'am and the Joint List—parties that support terrorism and reject the existence of the Jewish state." NETANYAHU DEFIES EXIT POLLS AS VOTE SHIFTS IN HIS FAVOR, BUT MAJORITY REMAINS ELUSIVE "A clear majority in the Jewish public chose the Likud as the largest party and me, as prime minister, to lead the next government. We aspire to form a broad government with our partners and with any party that wishes to do so and does not support terrorism. I am open to holding discussions on the matter," he added. The two predominantly Arab parties he pointed his criticism at are the Joint List and Ra'am who secured a historic combined total of 19 seats, potentially positioning them as kingmakers in the government formation process. "We said that if you want us not to attack Russia's refineries, they have not to attack our energy system." POLISH PRESIDENT TURNS PLANE AROUND AFTER 'COUP' AT NATION’S TOP COURT The dispute is also triggering diplomatic fallout, with at least three Polish ambassadors resigning in protest. items.summary_original: Ukraine officials said the country’s official air-raid alert app was likely hacked after emergency alerts warned on Sunday that there was a "radiation hazard" and a "chemical attack alert" in Kyiv. The false warnings urged residents not to go outside. "There is a radiation hazard alert in Kyiv. Do not go outside!" read one alert. RUSSIA LAUNCHES BALLISTIC MISSILE ATTACK ON KYIV HOURS AFTER ZELENSKYY WARNS OF MAJOR STRIKE "There is a chemical attack alert in Kyiv. Do not go outside!" another one read. The public air alert online map also displayed Kyiv and other areas as under a nuclear alert. The app also issued false warnings about Russia’s hypersonic Oreshnik missile and alleged street fighting in Kyiv. Additionally, loudspeakers in the streets blasted a recorded message instructing people to take precautions. But Ukraine’s Air Force said its air alert app was hacked and that there was no radiation hazard to be concerned about. "The air alert app appears to have been subjected to enemy influence. There is no radiation threat! Stay calm and follow our updates on our channel!" the Ukrainian Air Force said in a statement posted to Telegram. Ukraine’s Center for Strategic Communications blamed Russia for the incident, although no group had publicly claimed responsibility. items.summary_original: President Abelardo de la Espriella means business when it comes to his war against the cartels. Colombia's new president, known by the nickname of "El Tigre." was voted in on a law-and-order ticket and so far his actions in fighting the cartels are seemingly paying dividends — not just in Colombia but in Washington, too. Recently, he arrived at the Barranquilla police command around the early hours of the morning as 587 police officers and soldiers raided 50 locations across the Caribbean port city and its suburbs in Operation Blindaje 360. A few days earlier, domestic Colombian news outlets had widely publicized a recording intercepted by Colombian police of "Keko," the alleged leader of a gang called "Los del Freseo," boasting that de la Espirella had nothing on him. "The Tiger's got nothing. Let him come out, and we'll put lead in him," Keko allegedly said on the recording. Then, before dawn, Colombia's president had tracked him down and was face to face with him, all caught on tape. According to a video released by his presidential office, El Tigre told Keko the gang leader was "a tough guy on the phone… but the look of the fear on his face matched that of his many victims." The sweep ended with 72 arrests. items.summary_original: The U.S. Embassy in Moscow issued a security alert Saturday warning people of a potential "mass casualty event" at the 2 Museum Reserve in Moscow. "The U.S. Embassy in Moscow is aware of a credible threat of a mass casualty event TODAY October 31, at the Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve in Moscow at Dolskaya Ulitsa 1, Moscow, Russia 11569. The U.S. government is coordinating with appropriate Russian authorities on a response," the embassy wrote in a statement. The alert warned people to avoid the Tsaritsyno Museum area and to "stay alert, and avoid crowds." Founded in 1775 as a summer home for Russia's Catherine II, the Tsaritsyno Museum is now a popular tourist attraction in Russia's capital. INSIDE MELANIA TRUMP'S SECRET DIPLOMATIC ROLE IN THE RUSSIA-UKRAINE CEASEFIRE DEAL The museum itself attracted more than 2 million visitors in 2022, Moscow's deputy mayor, Natalya Sergunina, said in 2023. The surrounding grounds, enjoyed by Moscow's local citizens for physical activity and dog walking, get even more foot traffic, according to The Art Newspaper. The U.S. Embassy's alert also included a warning to people in the Moscow area to keep cellphone batteries and other batteries charged, remain aware of surroundings and review a personal security plan. The alert was issued as tensions in the ongoing war between Russia and Ukraine continue to escalate. items.summary_original: The French government is deploying 70,000 police officers to cities across the country as authorities expect a third week of intense anti-government protests to resume Saturday. Demonstrators objecting to rising costs and President Emmanuel Macron's government have engaged in looting and damaging property, prompting the law enforcement surge, according to officials. "Everyone is on deck to ensure an extremely firm response to any trouble," Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said at a news conference early in the week. FRANCE ON EDGE WITH 70,000 POLICE DEPLOYED FOR UNREST AS AUTHORITIES PROBE SUSPECTED TERROR ATTACK NEAR PARIS The expected protests, coinciding with Halloween, introduce an additional element to authorities' response, and some protesters are expected to don Halloween masks to hide their identities. At least 150 planned gatherings across the country have been tracked and acknowledged by the Interior Ministry. Videos circulating on social media Saturday appeared to show fresh confrontations as anti-government protests continued across France despite the deployment of 70,000 police officers nationwide. In Paris, video posted to X by journalist Oliya Scootercaster appeared to show an object being thrown toward a group of riot police as officers moved through a street. Scootercaster identified the object as a Molotov cocktail. A separate video shared on X by the account Bleu Blanc Rouge purported to show protesters breaking into a residential building in Marseille. items.summary_original: While en route to Senegal, Poland’s President Karol Nawrocki turned his plane around and returned home after police entered Poland's top court, the Constitutional Tribunal, and the tribunal’s president was suspended. "At such a moment, the President must be in Poland," Nawrocki posted on X . "I'm interrupting my flight to Senegal. I'm returning." Police say they secured the Tribunal after dozens of protesters gathered to demonstrate against what they called the wrongful suspension of the top court’s president by the current pro-European government. Police said there were also dangerous objects thrown at officers outside the building. Some protesters outside the court were seen praying, while others held posters reading "Tusk — a symbol of anti-Polish sentiment," "Down with the commies and Tusk’s regime," and "Stop destroying the state." Poland’s top judicial bodies, including the Constitutional Tribunal, have been a major bone of contention between the current pro-European government, led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk, and the main opposition party, national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), which ruled the country from 2015 to 2023. Critics accuse the PiS of imposing political control over key judicial institutions, with some reforms having led the EU to impose fines on Poland. items.summary_original: Israel's final election count has confirmed that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc has lost its parliamentary majority, but whether opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot can assemble a government to replace him remains an open question as negotiations begin behind closed doors. The completed count, published early Friday by Israel's Central Elections Committee , gave Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, compared with 48 for Eisenkot's opposition alliance. The two predominantly Arab parties secured a historic 19 seats, placing them in a potentially decisive position. Netanyahu's Likud emerged as the largest individual party with 27 seats, followed by Eisenkot's Yashar with 21 and former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett's Beyachad with 12. Final voter turnout reached 77.9%, according to the Central Elections Committee results . ISRAEL HEADS INTO DEEPLY DIVIDED ELECTION AS OCT. 7 RECKONING LOOMS: WHAT TO KNOW But the numbers leave neither major bloc with the 61 seats required for a majority, opening a complex political struggle involving potential partnerships with Arab parties, ultra-Orthodox lawmakers or a unity government bringing together longtime rivals. A source familiar with opposition discussions, who spoke to Fox News Digital on condition of anonymity, described the outcome as a "bitter stalemate," but not an impossible political situation. items.summary_original: Opposition lawmakers in Albania disrupted a parliamentary session on Thursday by setting off flares that filled the chamber with colored smoke, marking an escalation following weeks of student-led anti-government protests . Members of the main opposition Democratic Party also blocked access to the podium during a vote on a central bank bill, Reuters reported. "These ruling lawmakers are criminals, and they deserve tear gas, rubber bullets, cracked skulls, and broken bones—not the young people," opposition leader Sali Berisha declared during a speech before his microphone was cut off. SERBIA’S STUDENT MOVEMENT TOPPLES VUCIC’S PARTY AFTER 14 YEARS, BUT POLITICAL AGENDA REMAINS UNCLEAR As the chamber devolved into chaos, fellow opposition members surrounded Berisha, holding blue flares, the official color of their party, and displaying images of protesters injured by police rubber bullets. Albania has been gripped in recent weeks by student-led demonstrations demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama over alleged government corruption, underfunded schools, widespread unemployment, and a lack of economic opportunities. items.summary_original: Communist revolutionaries, socialist activists and pro-Palestinian agitators from a network of 106 organizations are preparing to stage a carefully choreographed spectacle of global unrest Friday at ports from Oakland, Calif., to Mumbai, India, as they protest Israel and "capitalist barbarism." A Fox News Digital investigation reveals that, far from a spontaneous eruption of outrage, the worldwide mobilization has been meticulously organized, with groups in the so-called "red-green" alliance of communist, socialist and pro-Palestinian movements spending the past week coordinating strikes, demonstrations and publicity around a common international playbook. Organizers are targeting 113 ports across 22 countries and regions on five continents, seeking to transform the world's commercial shipping hubs into stages for a synchronized show of opposition to Israel, NATO, Western military policies and the global capitalist system. CHAOS INC.: COMMUNISTS, PRO-PALESTINE AGITATORS IN THE RED-GREEN ALLIANCE, NOW IN OCT. 30 PORT PROTESTS The planned mobilizations – framed as "No Harbour for Genocide" with a sophisticated online tracker – stretches from Genoa and Livorno, Italy, to Piraeus, Greece, near Athens; Hamburg, Germany; Tangier, Morocco; Veracruz, Mexico; and Oakland and Marseille. The geographic sweep is part of the strategy, synchronizing actions across continents, giving them a common message and turning scattered demonstrations into the appearance of a worldwide uprising. items.title: بی‌طرفی، راستی‌آزمایی و پاسخ‌گویی؛ چرا بی‌بی‌سی فارسی بر این اصول ایستادگی می‌کند؟
items.summary: این مطلب توضیح می‌دهد که چرا بی‌بی‌سی فارسی در یکی از پرتنش‌ترین دوره‌های تاریخ معاصر ایران بر اصول بنیادین روزنامه‌نگاری، از جمله بی‌طرفی، راستی‌آزمایی، استقلال تحریریه و پاسخ‌گویی، پافشاری می‌کند. در این مقاله، با مرور شیوه تصمیم‌گیری‌های تحریریه، فرآیند راستی‌آزمایی اخبار، نحوه انتخاب مهمانان و برخورد با خطاها و انتقادها، تشریح می‌شود که هدف بی‌بی‌سی نه جانبداری از هیچ طرف، بلکه ارائه گزارشی دقیق، مستقل و مبتنی بر شواهد است تا مخاطبان بتوانند بر اساس اطلاعات قابل اعتماد، خود درباره رویدادها قضاوت کنند.
